junction.name: Rainier Avenue South & 25th Avenue South, Seattle

claims.text: Rainier Avenue South & 25th Avenue South had 77 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.3 million a year.
22% of crashes here were recorded as “rear ended” crashes, against 13% at the city's worst crash locations.
16% of crashes here were recorded as “from same direction - both going straight - one stopped - rear-end” crashes, against 9% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.
Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons would avoid about 2.4 crashes a year (CMF 9024, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $811,000 a year.

Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 1.8 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $609,000 a year; check on site: the pavement's friction is low now (wet-road crashes alone do not show it).
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for Rainier Avenue South (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
